comparator.name: Pharmacy (Farmacie)
comparator.sourceNotes: The Farmacie study path comprises a 135 EC required major and 45 EC of electives with the 7.5 EC bachelor thesis. The 15 EC thesis option instead yields a 142.5 EC major and 37.5 EC of electives. The example uses the first placement pattern in the official route table. The two patterns organise course enrolment and lead to the same curriculum. All three Academic Skills modules carry zero credits and are required. Passing the year-one module releases the credits for Onderzoek naar geneesmiddelen.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target is Pharmacy/Farmacie and the official current curriculum explicitly distinguishes the usual Farmacie study path from the separate Farmaceutische Wetenschappen path. The exact target-named Farmacie path is therefore reconstructed independently of UCR fit.

core: Molecular and cellular biology, biochemistry, human physiology, disease mechanisms and experimental investigation
Drug action, movement through the body, therapeutic use, toxicity, interactions and medicine safety
Laboratory, epidemiological, statistical and evidence-synthesis methods for medicine research and evaluation
adjacent: Quantitative modelling, data analysis and machine learning for drug action and treatment evidence
Safe medicine use, health behaviour, treatment decisions and the patient-facing role of pharmacy

trace: Develops heuristic search, optimisation and constraint satisfaction with transferable quantitative applications.
Develops data cleaning, visualisation and project-based analysis using R.
Implements regression, classification, resampling and clustering for prediction in biomedical and treatment data.
Develops neural networks for modelling complex data and evaluates predictions across tasks such as vision and time series.
Establishes programming, testing and computational problem-solving for reproducible biomedical-data workflows.
Establishes calculus and differential-equation methods for concentration, response and dynamic biological processes.
Develops matrix, vector and eigenvalue methods for multivariable biological and pharmacological models.
Uses numerical equation solving, integration and differential-equation methods that can be applied to concentration and response models.
Extends calculus to multiple dimensions and differential equations and uses computer algebra in analysis.
Studies linear system responses, convolution, Fourier analysis and filtering, providing transferable tools for signals and dynamic systems.
Develops probability, estimation and simulation for uncertainty, dose-response evidence and biomedical measurement.
Studies disease frequency, risk, screening and causal evidence for population-level assessment of treatment effectiveness and safety.
Connects anatomical structure with organ-system function and medical imaging, locating medicine effects within the human body.
Directly studies drug targets, pharmacokinetics, therapeutic use, toxicity and quantitative concentration-response relationships.
Studies immune recognition, host-pathogen interactions and immunopathology as disease mechanisms and treatment targets.
Derives pathophysiology across organ systems from anatomy and physiology, supporting rational therapeutic intervention.
Studies neurobiology, disorders, animal models, laboratory techniques and research ethics as a biomedical application domain.
Introduces macromolecules, DNA, cells, signalling and physiology as the biological foundation for pharmacology and disease study.
Introduces brain structure, learning and behaviour and provides the foundation for advanced psychology and evidence synthesis.
Studies cell structure, signalling, gene regulation, membranes and cellular mechanisms relevant to drug targets.
Studies homeostasis, signalling and integrated organ-system physiology needed to understand medicine effects.
Studies biomolecule chemistry, metabolism and molecular dysfunction without replacing pharmaceutical or organic chemistry.
Practises biochemical and molecular laboratory methods with proteins, DNA, bacteria, bioinformatics and diagnostic cases.
Studies molecular pathology, genetic disease, testing and treatment as mechanisms linking biological discovery to intervention.
Develops regression, multivariate analysis and experimental inference for health and treatment-response evidence.
Studies biological, psychological and social influences on illness, treatment behaviour and interventions in medical settings.
Performs systematic review and meta-analysis in R to estimate treatment effects and assess consistency.
Develops explicit ethical reasoning for evaluating responsibility, benefit, harm and fairness in health-related decisions.

alternatives.label: Pharmacology, Disease and Biomedical Research
alternatives.concept: Study how drugs act on the body and how disease changes the response to treatment. Combine pharmacology with anatomy, physiology, immunology, molecular pathology and laboratory research.
alternatives.labelReason: Pharmacology, physiology, laboratory science and disease mechanisms form the core, supported by health research and ethics.
progression: Biomedical foundations precede laboratory work, anatomy, physiology, pathology and pharmacology. Statistical and experimental methods prepare students for evidence synthesis.

alternatives.label: Pharmacology, Modelling and Health Data
alternatives.concept: Study drug action and disease mechanisms alongside quantitative tools. Use numerical methods, statistics and machine learning to ask how health data and mathematical models can inform research.
alternatives.labelReason: Pharmacology and disease mechanisms give context to numerical modelling, statistics and machine learning.
progression: Biomedical and mathematical foundations precede pharmacology, disease mechanisms, numerical modelling and advanced data analysis. Programming and machine learning precede advanced optimisation and neural networks.
alternatives.distinctness: Adds linear algebra, linear systems, advanced calculus, optimisation and neural networks. The closest option gives more space to anatomy, immunology, neurobiology, health psychology and ethics.

candidates.label: Quantitative pharmacology, drug movement and treatment evidence
candidates.reason: Drug action and kinetics provide the scientific anchor, supported by mathematical and computational methods for health research. The data courses teach transferable methods rather than clinical treatment decisions.

candidates.label: Patient-facing pharmacy and medicine-use practice
candidates.reason: Medical & Health Psychology studies consultation and shared decisions, and Ethics provides general normative reasoning. UCR lacks the formulation, dispensing and patient-specific medication review needed for a separate pharmacy practice option.

selection.assessment: The closest option supports drug action, disease mechanisms and experimental research. The quantitative option shares pharmacology and adds a distinct mathematical and computational sequence. General health psychology and ethics support some medicine-use questions without establishing a patient-facing pharmacy practice option.

blocks: Both address cellular and molecular mechanisms relevant to biological medicines; UCR does not reproduce pharmaceutical biotechnology or product development.
Both address endocrine physiology; UCR studies integrated human physiology rather than the complete pharmacy disease block.
Both involve experimental investigation; UCR supplies a broad life-science laboratory rather than medicine-specific pharmaceutical research.
UCR molecular pathology and genetics directly address neoplasia and cancer mechanisms, but not oncology pharmacotherapy as a complete block.
Both directly study infection and immune defence; the external course integrates these subjects with pharmacy.
Both address cardiovascular pathophysiology; UCR does not reproduce pharmaceutical treatment training.
The pharmacy skin-disease block remains visible; UCR has no dedicated dermatology or dermatological-pharmacy course.
Utrecht applies chronic inflammatory and autoimmune mechanisms to pharmacotherapy. UCR studies immune mechanisms in Infection & Immunity.
UCR Neurobiology and Pharmacology are each aligned once; there is no dedicated psychopharmacology course.
Utrecht introduces the pharmacy discipline and practice. UCR introduces cells, genetics and physiology in a separate biomedical course.
Utrecht studies neurological diseases and treatment. UCR Neurobiology provides nervous-system foundations and comparative approaches.
Medicine action, safety and health behaviour
Both directly study drug targets, mechanisms, pharmacokinetics, therapeutic use and toxicity.
UCR Pharmacology addresses pharmacokinetics once; the external dedicated kinetics block remains separately visible.
The integrated pharmacy therapy block remains visible; UCR disease and pharmacology courses do not reproduce clinical pharmacotherapy.
UCR does not offer dedicated medicine-administration or dosage-form training.
Pharmaceutical chemistry, product care, practice and profiling
UCR Biochemistry does not replace pharmaceutical chemistry.
Utrecht applies formulation, preparation, quality and analysis in product care.
The genuine 7.5-EC external profiling space is preserved without invented content.
The genuine 22.5-EC external profiling space is preserved without invented content.
Utrecht requires a bachelor thesis. UCR offers optional independent research in addition to the scheduled courses.
The genuine 15-EC external profiling space is preserved without invented content.

notes.text: The UCR options develop pharmacology, biomedical science and research skills. Utrecht also requires pharmaceutical chemistry, formulation, product care and disease-specific pharmacy work.

audience.programmeDescription: Utrecht’s Pharmacy bachelor studies how medicines are designed, prepared and used, how they act in the body and how their safety and effectiveness are assessed. This example follows the Farmacie study path.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The two UCR options connect pharmacology and disease mechanisms with either laboratory research or mathematical modelling and health data. Utrecht provides a more extensive sequence in pharmaceutical chemistry, formulation, product care and pharmacotherapy.

curriculum.limitation: All three Academic Skills modules are required and carry no credit. Students complete the required first-year courses before taking required advanced courses.
